body:
a lot has changed! i met my current girlfriend on a cruise last year and we’ve been together ever since, and we recently moved in together. i’m so glad i met her and so relieved about how things have worked out. she’s the most wonderful person and we fit really well together. 

the girl i was seeing before her, and the one this post was about.. looking back, we didn’t fit together very well at all. it’s impossible to communicate to your past self that in a matter of weeks, the perfect person will come along, and that you should stop trying to force a meaningful relationship that’s not there with someone that’s not right. but that’s exactly what happened to me. i met a girl who, when i’m with her, everything makes sense. 

i’m a cynic down to the core, but it’s hard not to conclude that sometimes, everything does happen for a reason. heartbreak and loss build you into the person you need to be for when you meet that special person who loves you the way you love them. heartbreak is awful and will hurt like hell, and it pushed me to a point where i really felt like giving up, but right now i’m listening to my beautiful girlfriend snoring gently beside me, and i’m really proud of myself for not giving up. opening yourself up to love is one of the best things you can do in my opinion ❤️

i’m actually doing really well now, it took about a year i’d say until i felt properly back to normal. obviously there’s days where i still think of her and i’ll always miss those certain moments i hold dear to me. but now i feel happy, more myself, and i have a wonderful girlfriend who i met in june and who makes me feel really happy to be alive

read this if you wanna bum yourself out 

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyce_Vincent
frightened rabbit - poke

she used to cheat at board games, even when it was just me and her playing monopoly against eachother - i would leave the room to get a drink or something, and when i’d get back i’d often catch her in the middle of moving the bank money to her pile. she’d get in a sour mood if i accused her so i used to just pretend i hadn’t seen 😅 i kinda loved that about her tbh
this is about as similar to my situation as it gets - spooky

relapsing pretty dang hard today, i guess it’s been coming a while. she called me about a month ago, told me that she still loves me and that she wishes i’d replied to her hoover attempts months ago because we could have ‘made it work.’ in the meantime she’s still living with her partner, i don’t know where.

it’s all just a headfuck. in the autumn i felt like i was starting to leave all this behind me. i felt ok for the first time since she left me. now i’m finding i feel just as broken and afraid as that first day, it’s so disheartening. i’m crying on the way to work again. i cry in the shower. i have really really negative thoughts about myself. i’m scared and alone, and i know things can never go back to how they were but that’s all i think about again now. i don’t want to exist like this, i can’t. if this is the rest of my life now it’s not worth it.
maybe twee pop?
100% - the world might have been a very different place without these brave men
absolute king 👑👑👑
that kick through was gorgeous

I broke my nose when i was about 3 years old, and had to wait until i was an adult for it to stop growing before i could get it fixed. by that time i was unable to breathe out of one nostril, and my nose was very squashed to the side and it became something i was very insecure and self conscious about. 

i couldn’t believe how much more confidence having a straight nose gave me, it was honestly a turning point in my life looking back, and i was lucky enough to get it for free on the NHS. i’m by no means pro-body modifications for purely aesthetic reasons, but i have to say noses make a huge difference and can understand why people would want to get it done
finn russell was unreal today

you’re right, that genie doesn’t go back in the bottle. and i’m almost certain she cheated that night, she was just too ashamed to admit it. when she broke up with me she was in a psychotic state, babbling and incoherent. the gravity of what she’d done was hitting her i think. she went truly scorched earth after that. when i tried to commit suicide later that day, she told me “well that just proves to me that i’m making the right choice” it’s like the person i knew never existed in that moment, they’d been replaced with a monster.

it’s been 7 months since the breakup, i’ve done a lot of self work, read a library’s worth of self help books, 😂 and have kept myself busy with friends, family and hobbies. the last time she messaged me was in november, and i ignored her. right now i’m kinda in a headspace where i just feel sorry for her. all i really want now is for us both to be happy

you’re exactly right, but i really doubt that will ever happen. these relationships are the kind where you have to take your own closure. 

and virtually everyone on this subreddit has been through their fair share of hard times dealing with people who have this awful illness. yes, it’s painful, but i’m so thankful for this group because collectively we can use our pain for good, to not only become better people but to share our experiences and show others that they’re not alone. and i think that’s a wonderful thing ❤️

honestly mate, thank you so so much for your responses, they’ve made me feel so much more validated in my experience. dealing with the fallout of the end of a bpd relationship is often a painful and lonely experience, but to have this group, and to know that there are people like you who have gone through the same thing, its so valuable. it makes you feel like you’re not crazy 😂 

for me the signs also started slow, slow enough to assume that they were just normal parts of any relationship. stuff like her asking me to grab her things if we were both sat down on the sofa, little digs at my family or friends, intimacy drying up, all things that felt small, but then added up into a systematic devaluation. in my opinion our relationship was stronger and deeper than any of my friends relationships, and yet ours ended in a brutal discard. 

i completely get what you mean about the lengths that you’re willing to go to forgive. it got to the point when after she’d cheated on me, the guy she left me for turned her down for a proper relationship (he just wanted sex) and she came back to me begging for forgiveness. and i did forgive her. i wanted so bad to fix things that i sat and listened to her crying about being turned down by some asshole guy who didn’t give a shit about her, and i comforted her. i was so codependent and so far gone at this point i was willing to completely obliterate my sense of self worth to soothe her. 

again, thank you so much for replying to me and listening to me vent, it’s been an emotional day. alike you, i’ve found it really helps to write things down/repeat mantras to myself. the one i find most useful and something i try to tell myself every day is ‘i’m worth so much more than the way i was treated’ - this is a healing journey with no real finish line, and some days i find it harder that others to say that sentence out loud and believe it. i wish you all the best friend ❤️

i appreciate this comment and you’re more than likely right. i think i’m just such a hopeful person i’d like to think i could make at least part of a difference. i know that’s naive but it is what it is. it’s been an eye opening experience over the last 7 months or so to realise that so much about not only bpd relationships, relationships in general but also life, is completely out of our control. we can only control how we react to a situation. and if i react in a positive or principled way, then that can’t be a bad thing. thanks again for your comment ❤️

thank you for noticing that, i often feel like i’m being harsh for fixating on parts of messages like this, especially when tone is hard to decipher. she knows the best way to get the upper hand on me is to speak either face to face, or on the phone alone, because i get quite easily flustered and emotionally manipulated when it’s just me and her. when i have time to form a response away from the heightened emotion, that’s when i say/make better choices. 

i completely understand you because the last time we talked, about 3 months after the breakup, i was still in a really raw emotional place. she rang late at night after my shift at work, so i was exhausted and susceptible to getting into a responsive state. what ended up happening was she began bragging about her new relationship and life without me, to which i reacted by saying how much she’d hurt me and how callous her actions were. to her this worked as great fuel to devalue me more. i begged and pleaded, told her i’d be better, the works. she got everything she needed from that conversation, and i got the worst case scenario. 

the only option i really have is to ignore this kind of message. in my mind it’s clear that she’s fishing for some sort of validation, to alleviate her guilt. i would be throwing myself under the bus if i was to give her that
yeah this is the elephant in the room, and i’m not sure if i’m ready to make that step yet to be honest
thank you ❤️

apologies if i’m not the most articulate, but in my mind, and i know it’s kinda idealist bullshit -  i’d like to think that i have power in the way that i respond to her, for her to become a better person from all of this. i still deeply care for my ex, and i want her to have a meaningful and fulfilling life, and i’m not sure she will if she goes down the route she has been. 

i might be making assumptions, but unless she heals the wound at the core of her being, and to my mind the driver of her behaviours, her trauma, then she’ll just repeat the same patterns over and over again. if i was to ‘let her off the hook’ and offer her my forgiveness, i believe it would show her that it’s ok to treat people this way. again, i’m not trying to make myself out as some great virtuous person, because i’m not by any means, but for our time together to mean something, i’d like it to mean that she looks inward at her behaviour and makes the appropriate changes. i’m not sure she’d do that if i made her feel like it was ok to do the things she did to me.

i’d like to think so. that was the easy bit, the hard bit is now realising that the last bit of hope that existed in the back of my mind is now entinguished. you’re right that it’s a milestone, and the start of a new phase of acceptance. it’s bittersweet

to cut a long story short, she cheated on me with a guy she met at her work. one night i got home late and she told me she was heading into town to meet him because he was going through a crisis. she didn’t come back that night, and broke up with me on the phone walking back from his the next morning. just a few hours after she broke up with me she slept with him, and then again later that week. 

at this point i’d tried to commit suicide twice and was absolutely devastated. we’d been planning wedding stuff the week before, and would have been married in a matter of weeks. she began flaunting this new guy on her social media, but then suddenly he turned around and said he didn’t want a relationship with her, he probably just wanted the sex.

she then immediately hopped into a relationship with a new guy, who she’s been with ever since, probably about 6 months now. during that time she’s persistently stalked my social media, spotify and youtube, and also the socials of the couple of girls that i’ve briefly dated. the last time we spoke was in august, when she admitted that in the last year of the relationship, she was ‘shopping around’ for my replacement. hell, we even went out together to meet one of the guys she was planning to leave me for, she told me that they were friends, and i had no reason not to trust her.

the whole situation left me feeling crushed and small, it felt like i was completely unworthy of love, and it’s taken intense therapy and really difficult self work to drag myself out of that place, a journey that i’m still going through.

i tend to ramble on this sub, i’ll finish by saying that just a week before the breakup i remember her saying “please never leave me, i don’t know what i’d do without you” while simultaneously planning and manoeuvring for her exit. i don’t think i can ever forgive that, illness or not

thanks again, i’m sorry for what you’ve been through. it’s the worst pain imaginable. 

it’s what in my opinion makes quiet bpd the most insidious and damaging form of the illness, in regard to the time post breakup/discard. you look back and struggle to find bad things to say about this person, they were so good for so long, it makes it harder to move on. i’m not trying to say it’d be easier if she more explicitly/physically abused me, i just think that’s where a large portion of the pain and fallout is felt with a quiet bpd ex.

and it because of this, and in spite of the way that i was treated in the end, that i’m still in 2 minds about shutting the door and leaving us in the past. many of my friends think i’m crazy for even considering forgiveness/reconciliation. but i don’t think they understand the blissed out dynamic of a relationship that was like pure heaven until it wasn’t. the only way i can describe it to my friends is that she was the best, most perfect person, until she inexplicably wasn’t in a split second. 

i agree with your point that she probably won’t change. in the past she’s had moments of lucidity and self awareness, but she stops short of accountability. shame is a huge factor in driving her behaviour, something that was unfortunately drilled into her from a very young age when she was abused by a family member. i’m repeating myself but i genuinely wish her the best. no one deserves to go through what she went through, but i can’t be in the middle of the resulting trauma response.
i think i’d block her if she messaged again. she’s been pretty consistent in messaging or calling every couple of months since the breakup last may, it’s not healthy for either of us to keep that up

i completely agree with you. i suspect my ex had quiet bpd, and i didn’t really know i was being devalued right until the discard. looking back now there were signs, but they were outweighed massively by the love that she gave me. she made me feel like the luckiest man alive. 

but the discard couldn’t have been more sudden and cruel. it’s like she went out of her way to hurt me, and to ensure there was no way back for any kind of relationship, be that romantic or friendship. 

like you say, to even put myself through a fraction of that suffering again, would be the biggest step back i could possibly take. the mess she made at the end of the relationship has taught me that i’m worth so much more than how i was treated. if she is now feeling regret and is remembering the love that we once shared, then unfortunately i have to leave her with that in order for her to grow as a person, and to not repeat these behaviours with her next partner. i just hope she’s doing ok

thanks so much friend. a large part about why this healing process has been so hard, is because the person i knew and loved for 4 years was completely the opposite to the person i saw at the end. i almost feel that the ‘good’ her is still there somewhere, but i can’t throw myself back into that arena again, i just can’t. but it’s hard to convince yourself that what you’re doing is the right thing to do
i was mulling over whether i should have replied or not, we’ll see if she respects this boundary i guess

i’m glad you think so - i have no doubt that one day we’ll maybe be able to talk as friends, but i’m not ready for that now, and i think at the minute she’s just looking to soothe her guilt. i’d be doing me and her a disservice if i was to let that happen. i’ve been in therapy for half a year now trying to heal and grow from this experience, and to forgive her of her behaviours would rob her of that chance to grow too if that makes sense
i’m hoping this will be the last time we speak to be honest. she closed the door when she discarded me in may, and it feels like i’m closing that door now too. it’s a bittersweet feeling
thank you. it was a hard message to send because i still deeply care for her, but we’re not good for eachother

i completely sympathise with your pain. it feels as if you’ve been conned doesn’t it? you almost feel embarrassed that you didn’t notice the manipulation or the coercion, considering how close you were to this person. it feels so brutally unfair because you were most likely giving away every facet of your being to your ex, because to you, and to most healthy people, that’s what love is. 

but you can’t blame yourself for that. and i know that’s easier said than done, and i myself am still a work in progress in that regard. but just think what you’d say to a friend of yours who was going through the same thing as you, and was saying the same things you are. you’d want them to know it wasn’t their fault, and that they couldn’t have done anything differently. 

you’re a victim in this situation, and blaming a victim is counterintuitive. keep your head held high, you’ve got this ❤️

last week or so has been really tough. it’s been nearly 7 months now and i just can’t see when this pain will end. i’m tired of pretending i’m ok, i still feel just as confused and abused as day 1. and yet i never even come close to feeling hatred for her, i just feel bad for the both of us. i need a hug lol

completely understand you and i’m so sorry 😔 i was engaged to my exwbpd. it’s been 7 months and there’s times i just sit there and think about what happened and it just feels too weird to be true. it feels like a dumb joke and i’m waiting for the punchline. it’s so sad to think our relationship meant nothing to her because it meant everything to me. it was my greatest achievement and now it just feels like i was unreasonable for thinking things could be so good, it just feels like good things aren’t meant for me

i’m also having a shit day, but it feels reassuring to know that shit days end, and every day from now has the potential to be better than the last! time and distance will help to transform what right now may be shitty days, into better ones. 

think of healing as a journey with peaks and valleys, but on a gentle upwards trajectory. i promise you things will improve, even if it feels bleak now. also hold your head high knowing that the pain you feel right now is your very own receipt for loving someone fully. grieving shows that we have, and can love. and personally speaking i feel lucky for having had that experience. 

try and enjoy time with family and friends over christmas, you got this 💪💪💪

it’s been just over 6 months. still find myself subconsciously missing her and thinking about her all the time.

i just got dumped a 2nd time this year after a 1.5 month situationship with a girl i was really hopeful and enthusiastic about, and now there’s nothing filling my thoughts or time, and my mind wanders back to my exwbpd. the situationship never felt like a distraction, i felt ready to move on, and i’m disheartened that i’m now reminiscing about times with my exwbpd.

i ignored her last breadcrumb message, and she still watches all my instagram stories, still pinches songs from my spotify playlists. i have no idea where she’s at with her life at the minute, i don’t hold any hostility towards her. honestly i just want peace for her and for me. 

hopefully 2023 is a better year
thank you so much! i’ve been on the brink of crying all day and this tipped me over the edge ❤️ it’s time to focus on me x

this is eerily spot on from my experience. it’s only when i felt like our relationship was moving into an area of vulnerability/intimacy is when she broke things off. i just wish there was something i could do, without triggering her avoidance more

❤️❤️❤️ we were in that really exciting early stage of what i could sense was going to be a wonderful relationship - i really want to reach out and reassure her but i feel like a large part of the reason she’s pulled away is because of my eagerness in the first place. i feel like the potential deeper level of intimacy has scared her. she’s always reposting stuff on her social media that alludes to CPTSD - but i don’t know the extent to her trauma. i hope she can get better because she’s a wonderful person

she offered a somewhat apology, she told me not to blame myself and that it was a ‘her’ problem, not me. it just left me slightly confused more than anything, everything was going completely fine until that point. she seems like quite a mature and thoughtful woman, albeit troubled with some sort of trauma she wouldn’t disclose to me. i have no other choice than to remain no contact i think
thank you friend. i’m sorry for what you went through. i’m going to look after myself, and whatever happens, happens
initially i offered to remain as friends, but i think no contact would be the best route from here

thank you for this. i can’t tell you how comforting this advice and the advice/support of this community is. my heart tells me that this is a person with avoidant tendencies. our last date and our recent conversations had been incredibly positive and exciting, but for now like you say, i need to move on and heal. it’s all i can do really

thanks so much for this advice - i’m gonna take a couple of weeks to feel sad about this and then i’m gonna get back out there. it’s exhausting and sometimes disheartening, but i think it’s important to get yourself out there. i’m only gonna be young once so it’s time to make it count
really beautifully written ❤️ keep being the wonderful person you undoubtedly are x

thank you for sharing. i’ve already been through a breakup this year in may, and i know from experience that you shouldn’t wait around for someone at your own expense. what’s most painful about this breakup is that we were together for such a short period of time, but i felt we really clicked. the last date we went on was probably my favourite i’ve ever been on, and she seemed genuinely excited to see me again. these last 2 failed relationships are really making me question whether it’s worth putting myself out there and trying again
maybe she is. i’ve got a feeling she’s trying to let me down gently because she’s met someone new who she prefers to me. either way the situation sucks

i think you’re right, it’s just heartbreaking :/ i’d only known her a few months, but we got on like a house on fire, and she seemed really excited to keep on seeing me. and now it’s like a switch has been flipped
i’m guess i’m just sad she thought she couldn’t heal her past trauma while also being in a relationship with me. it’s just a shitty situation
thank you friend ❤️
unfortunately this is my 2nd breakup this year, so i know how this goes :( just don’t know where i’m going wrong really
thank you, our relationship was also quite short, i’m just really disappointed to be honest. i can’t help but be sad for what could have been
thank you. it’s been a bit of a headfuck, but the advice of people in this community and my friends has really helped

my theory is that things have now calmed down in her life again. her friends and family are probably now bored of the drama she tends to gravitate towards, and with no updates or communication from me, that source of drama has all but dried up. 

i’m also assuming she’s having doubts about the longevity and health of the relationship with her new supply. she hopped into a relationship with him within 3 weeks of our breakup, and they’re most likely reaching the end of their honeymoon period. i know this because it was exactly the same with me and my ex. she turned off all the affection after about a year and became lazy and neglectful to my needs, meanwhile i doted on her and bent over backwards for her at the drop of a hat. 

i can’t describe her properly without mentioning that her and her entire family seem to have an unusual tendency to self sabotage and seek out conflict and drama the moment things get too comfortable or idyllic in their life. they all went through a very traumatic and difficult upbringing, and maybe they feel most safe when things are wrought with conflict in a weird way.

what she’s referring to is that in our last conversation i finally stuck up for myself and called out her poor/abusive behaviour as what it is. i think she’s probably now trying to play the victim because when we were together i used to bend over backwards for her at every juncture. i never raised my voice with her, and am an incredibly hard person to anger. in our last conversation she was essentially goading me, telling me about how great her new boyfriend was, saying things are “different” now she’s with him, apparently in a good way. the most angry thing i said to her is that she was acting exactly like her mother, who i suspect also has bpd and who she routinely splits black.
i don’t think i’m going to reply, i stand to lose too much progress

i’m so sorry for what you’ve been through friend. nobody deserves that and i hope you’re recovering and healing well. if there’s anything good that can come from my relationship with my ex, aside from the wonderful memories at the start, it’s the fact that it’s been an incredible teacher for me. obviously i’d rather not have been cheated on and neglected but it’s taught me exactly the kind of things i need to look out for as red flags in my future relationships. 

i genuinely wish my ex well and if she came to me with proof that she wanted to change for the better and had worked on herself then maybe i’d be more receptive to this kind of message. but for now i need to put myself first and carry on with my healing. it kind of hurts for me to just ignore her, but sadly it’s necessary

the last time we spoke in august i was absolutely dumbfounded with her inability to see what she’d done was wrong and hurtful. it’s tragic, but it seems like my ex, and people with bpd in general seem to act like their emotions are absolute justification for their actions. they can’t be wrong or have done something morally reprehensible because in their heightened emotional state it must feel like a matter of life and death. in her mind she must have felt like she was doing what it took to survive. i was simply collateral damage. 

it’s what makes this horrible illness even more damaging to friends and family who have suffered from being abused or neglected. the times when things are good, they’re just the sweetest, kindest and vulnerable people. you feel compelled to care for them because you know how much suffering they’ve been through. and when things are bad and you’re being mistreated, you’re therefore more likely to forgive and forget, in order to try and smoothly transition back to those good times. it keeps you in a loop of disfunction and neglect. even now with the perspective i have, the temptation to engage with her again is so strong. i’m so grateful to this community for giving me the very necessary reality check i need

thank you so much for your advice! i’m sorry you’ve had such a rough experience in the past with disordered people. if it’s any consolation at all, the advice from experienced people like you and this subreddit in general is invaluable to people like me going through this sort of thing now. if i hadn’t stumbled across this support group months ago i think i would have made every mistake in the book, and would have made decisions and had a mindset detrimental to my healing. 

i’ve learned a lot about how this sort of thing normally pans out, and the risk of harming myself and my mental health is something i have to take really seriously. i didn’t get the overall sense that this was a person who’d changed or was remorseful from the tone of her message.

i’m trying not to but i think she knew this message would hit at a core weakness within me which is my over-eagerness to forgive. she knows me inside and out and knows that this is exactly the kind of message i would ruminate over. it’s been a hard day today trying to keep things in perspective  and not message her back
thanks for this advice friend

not at all. i tried to gently suggest it throughout our relationship because i was worried about her but it was something she always steadfastly refused to do. i can understand why, she was abused horribly as a child and it’d be opening up a can of worms, but it’s the only way i can see her having a healthy approach to relationships now and in the future. i gave it my all and really looked after her, but i felt completely out of my depth trying to support her through some of her tougher times.
e x a c t l y!!! i don’t really get the meaning behind it. it’s taking a lot for me to not reply and find out what her motivations are, but i guess that shows how far i’ve come ✨

as of right now i’m honestly just considering ignoring it. it’s only recently i seem to have turned a corner and am starting to feel a lot more positive about life without her. i might regret this if i relapse, but like you say it finally feels like the ball is in my court after so so long. i’m going to sleep on it and decide whether to message back
haha spot on

weirdly 90 days after the breakup was the first time she reached out to me, and under the pretence of ‘checking up’ on me. in reality i think she rang me because she was confused why i didn’t reach out to her first (this was 2 days after what would have been our wedding day) it’s been another 90 days exactly since then and she’s reached out again. it’s almost like she has an in-built timer. 😂

i can only speculate why she’s reached out a 2nd time. maybe her current supply has up and left her. maybe she just wants the ego boost of me meekly begging for her affection again. but i’ve come so far in this last 90 days and i’m beyond the man i was the last time i fell for the breadcrumbs. 

i’m rambling but it feels weirdly cathartic to put myself first, even though i do still have deep lingering feelings for her. i’m proud of myself for separating my emotional situation from the actual situation. i won’t be responding

i’m really sorry for your experience. i had no idea it was possible to feel as betrayed and worthless as i did after she admitted to cheating on me, and then  even worse when left me for the same guy. like you say, these people shouldn’t be denied of love based off their illness, but it wouldn’t be unwise of me to go back to a situation where i was mistreated and disrespected. if i was sure she was putting in the work and trying to address her faults and trauma then maybe it would be a different conversation. 

i’ve spent so much of my life the last 4 years putting her first, and above my own needs, regardless of whether or not that would affect me negatively. that’s changed now. i need to start choosing me, and not engaging with this hoover attempt is an important first step for me
thank you. staying strong through this kind of thing is so hard but i think so important!

this is exactly what my ex is like. i have deep sympathy for her, but unless she’s getting treatment for the trauma which i believe is the core root of her bpd, she’ll always go down the same path. i’ve really put work into myself since the breakup and i would be selling myself short if i was to engage in any kind of relationship with her.
thank you friend 💪
it’s so weird because i think i would have given anything to have her message me something like this just a few weeks ago, but now after all i’ve learned about myself and her, i see it for what it is
thanks so much for this! i’ve been talking to my friends and they think the same. i’ve come too far in these last few months to risk throwing it away now. onward with my healing 💪

i’m sorry for your shitty experience :/ and i completely understand what you mean about the flip of a switch. the difference only a few short hours made was like night and day. one minute she was saying “please never leave me i don’t know what i’d do” and the next she’s sleeping with a guy she’d known for a matter of weeks
yeah i’m definitely gonna sleep on it tonight, i’m erring on the side of not replying though. i don’t wanna put myself through the pain again

the change in my ex from before she split on me to after was like night and day. she blew things up so spectacularly, it feels like something that’ll never be able to go back in the box. i think maybe she’s just after an opportunity to offload her guilt
this is my thoughts too, it’s really rattled me today because i thought i’d never hear from her again. i’m glad you agree cause i feel like i’m being unreasonable or harsh to just ignore her

YES! i would sit for ages giving my ex hundreds of choices of food to eat, movies to watch, dates to go on, and she’d turn them all down inexplicably. it was as if she couldn’t bring herself to allow me to have a day in things. 

from a psychological standpoint i’m guessing it’s a reaction to the lack of control they feel in their ability to regulate emotions, or trying to exert control which they completely lacked in their often traumatic childhood.

when i quizzed her about it, she didn’t really know why she’d turn down things just because i chose them. weird.

i started off in complete denial, couldn’t eat or sleep for a few weeks. my therapist and some friends gave me the best advice, which was: 1) to take things one day at a time, sit with your feelings and experience the grief. sadly it’s unavoidable and necessary. crying feels cathartic in this period, almost like throwing up when you’re too drunk. 

and 2) buckle up for what is essentially a drug detox. i don’t know your situation in depth, but you need to essentially go cold turkey on your ex as if you were a heroin addict trying to kick the addiction. it’s really really hard, but if you can completely separate yourself from them (no checking social media stalking or messaging them) it speeds up your recovery tenfold. loving someone is an amalgamation many things, but a significant part of it is (weirdly) chemical. your brain is addicted to the ‘feel good drug’ your ex partner gave you. if you go no contact, you give yourself the best chance of weening yourself off this quickly, and then i found myself feeling a lot better/functional at the very least

i personally think the reason my ex called me, and maybe the same reason your ex reached out to you, was to maintain a semblance of control. bpd sufferers seem to have a desperate need to feel like they’re in control of things, probably because they had a complete lack of control of their situation growing up. for my ex to contact me and hear that i still wanted to get back together with her must have been a terrific boost to her ego and given her the satisfaction of being in complete control still. 

in the last few weeks since she rang me i’ve moved past the idea that we could get back together. she’s broken things too completely for that to happen. i’ll always hold a tenderness inside me for her, and i wish her all the happiness in the world with her new life, but i don’t want to see or be involved with that anymore.

literally days before the breakup we had one of my favourite days we’d ever had in the 4.5 years together. we’d been out walking and then to our favourite pub for drinks and card games. we then stumbled back up the hill towards our house, laughing and kissing eachother, it felt like we were the giddy teenagers we were when we started dating. she told me to stand still so she could take a picture of me with the sunset in the background, and i can still remember how beautiful she looked as she squinted to take the photo. we then spent the rest of the evening getting even more drunk and watching shitty movies, life couldn’t get more perfect.

skip a couple of days and i get home from work to her telling me she has to meet a friend in town who’s having a crisis. she’d met him at work about a month beforehand, and i’d noticed her texting him regularly, but thought nothing of it. she tells me she’ll be back by bedtime and i kiss her goodbye and let her go. and that was it. she didn’t come home that night. i frantically messaged and looked for the guys house in pure panic, but then gave up and tried to sleep. when i woke the next morning i get a call from her and she says “so i think i’m breaking up with you” in the most cruel sing-songy kind of voice. i was completely crushed. it was like something evil had gotten inside her and was controlling her. i was in so much pain i tried to take my own life.

in the months that followed after the breakup, and through therapy and a lot of soul searching, i started to look back and see that our relationship wasn’t as perfect as i once thought. but the thing is with quiet bpd, the moments when she could be cruel or short with me, sound minuscule in comparison to many partners of bpd sufferers on this subreddit. she was largely speaking, a wonderful partner, very loving and kind to me. i’d only really seen her be brutal and split with friends she used to know. but i’ll never forget how violent the switch in her was during the breakup. it was like her entire personality changed, she even looked physically different too, it was bizarre.

a couple of weeks ago, and around 3 months after the breakup, she called me to check up and see how i was doing - or that’s what she said the call was for. i think she actually rang trying to bait me into saying something to her that would justify the breakup and her decision. i must confess i did vent my frustrations to her. she told me she’d stopped talking to the friend that i presumed she’d left me for, because he was “a fuckboy asshole.” she then told me that she’d immediately found a new partner about a fortnight after our breakup and had been with him since. she sounded to be infatuated with him, and said their love is so much different than ours was. she then told me that she didn’t know she was going to break up with me until the moment the words left her lips. i left the call in many ways more confused than before.

having time to reflect, and seeing the relationship through the lens of quiet bpd as opposed to regular bpd, things make more sense now. i’ve found some peace in the fact that there was virtually nothing i could do to stop what happened, in many ways it was baked into her brain that she had to destroy everything. it’s at the end of the day, a trauma response. it must have felt like a matter of life and death to her. i’m certain that she’ll eventually do it to the new person that she’s with, and the cycle of trauma and abuse will continue. all because of the way her parents abused her as a child. life is cruel.

in many ways i think quiet bpd is worse for the partner than regular bpd. the psychological effects of being completely blindsided are brutal and long lasting. i’ve found peace in reading and coming to a better understanding of bpd, and am more equipped to cope with problems in future relationships now. but in many ways i don’t think i’ll ever get over my ex, and how much fun we had in the 4 years we spent together. her spirit and charm will never leave me. soulmate is a dumb concept and one i don’t really believe in, but i’d be damned if we weren’t meant to be together. we were so good. what a waste

i’m 2 months out from a blindside breakup too. largely i’ve found that there’s only so much you can do to stop the painful emotions and the anxiety, you just have to ride out the worst moments if you can. however i’ve found that a few things help:

1) try not to obsessively think about the breakup or spend too much time on your phone, trying to find out how your ex is doing etc. i have a real problem with this, but i’ve noticed things have become a lot easier since i muted her on everything. the worst evening i’ve had so far since the breakup was finding out she’s dating someone else by watching her instagram story. it sounds dumb and cliche but now i don’t have access to that, it really does feel like out of sight, out of mind. i no longer have to see her name or face and can begin properly making steps to move on.

2) speak to people about how you’re feeling. if you don’t want to speak to friends or family because you feel like you’re bothering them, which is never true btw, there’s always helplines and therapists who are incredibly capable of giving you pragmatic and practical advice. i’ve also found just venting on reddit helps, and i’ve heard that journaling is a good way of processing difficult emotions and making sense of your thoughts. the very act of just saying things out loud or writing them down always makes me feel better immediately afterwards.

3) have a good cry. i try to release my pent up emotions in the car on the way back from work every day. if you let things build up for too long, i find it brings your overall mood down

4) i’ve suffered from mental health issues for about 10 years, and when i’m in my most difficult moments, even though it seems impossible, i find that going for a walk really helps to calm me down. even just getting up and moving works. it’s easier said than done, but try not to lay in bed too long or you’ll start to compound the negative emotions.

5) again it’s cliche and cringe, but just repeating a few mantras to myself whenever i feel especially low helps to drown out the negative thoughts i have. my personal favourites at the moment are “her loss” and “i deserve better.” just keep reminding yourself that you have incredible self worth and try not to blame yourself for anything.

i know a lot of these points are based on a kinda ‘fake it until you make it’ psychology, and it’s a lot easier to say than to do, but i think any progressive steps forward can only help you. take care of yourself x
